fields.statement: QA with a scratch build of this branch in a scratch git repo, hermetic HOME: a personal myflow.toml under ~/.config/rhiza/workflows (XDG_CONFIG_HOME unset) shadowed the repo's .rhiza/workflows/myflow.toml in workflow ls; with XDG_CONFIG_HOME set, the $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rhiza/workflows file won. Gave cmdonly a personal and a repo file, each a command step writing its layer name. run start --workflow cmdonly --foreground and a repo workflow 'outer' (a workflow step naming cmdonly) both ran the personal file (said.txt = layer-personal). Each run journal recorded workflow_path as the personal file's path (outer.toml for outer)

QA with a scratch build: workflow ls in a scratch repo listed the 4 built-ins as builtin:<name>. After adding repo and personal files it showed each name once with its winning layer and path, plus 'shadows repo <path>' and 'shadows builtin builtin:review' lines for review (personal > repo > builtin). workflow ls --json printed the same bytes as rhiza api call workflow.ls '{}' (cmp)

QA with a scratch build: workflow describe ship-change showed source builtin:ship-change, start build/build, includes build, review, and steps as <workflow>/<step> with kinds, on.* targets and roles with model ladders and prompts. A personal review shadowing repo and builtin showed both shadows lines. Editing the repo review.toml changed what ship-change's included review resolved to (shared resolver). describe left the file count under .git/rhiza and .rhiza unchanged (18 -> 18). --json was byte-identical to api call workflow.describe '{"workflow":"ship-change"}'

QA with a scratch build: workflow check on build, plan, review and ship-change and on testdata/valid.toml exited 0 ('is valid'). bad-outcome, missing-target and unknown-kind each exited 1 naming the step and the problem. A file with two bad steps reported both, in the same bytes across 8 runs. A workflow step naming a missing workflow 'ghost' was reported. --json was byte-identical to api call workflow.check

QA with a scratch build: workflow new sc --from ship-change wrote .rhiza/workflows/sc.toml, which diffs from internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml only in the name line and passes workflow check. workflow new myflow wrote a commented skeleton that passes check and runs under run start --workflow myflow --dry-run ('would start', nothing written). Re-running new on an existing name exited 3 with the file unchanged; a/b and x.toml exited 2; --dry-run printed 'would write' and created no file

QA with a scratch build: rhiza guide ls lists the workflows topic. rhiza guide workflows covers the personal/repo/built-in layers, every step kind and its keys (agent, wait, command, leaves, checks, signoff, arbiter, workflow), outcomes, the reserved targets done/failed, includes as <workflow>/<step>, and the ls/new/describe/check/run start --dry-run loop. I followed that loop by hand in a scratch repo and it worked as written
